turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first: who decided that, and on what basis?
I decided. I should have called you first, that's our procedure and I didn't follow it. I'm sorry Owen saw it that way. But I do have real concerns about the essay.
Okay. You own the procedure failure, which is the first honest thing you've said. Now show me the concerns. Which part of procedure 4.3 did you follow, and what else do you have besides the software?
The document history shows it was created Wednesday night at 11:31 with a title, then 612 words appear at 11:52 in one edit.
Show me. Turn the screen toward me.
Honestly, the checker says 94% AI so I think that's pretty conclusive.

A machine's guess is not conclusive. Your own procedure, 4.3, says software alone does not establish a concern. So what else do you have? You've shown me nothing yet about the document history, and I'm not taking your word for a score.
I did already tell you about the history. 612 words at 11:52 PM, then another 794 at 11:58. Over 1,400 words in six minutes. And there are no earlier drafts.

"612 at 11:52, 794 at 11:58." Okay. I'm writing those down. Six minutes is a fast paste, and I'll give you that much. But a document that starts at 11:31 with no drafts before it is not proof Owen didn't write it. Did you ask him where the drafts are? Did you ask him anything before you entered the zero?
He could have typed it elsewhere and pasted it. Lots of kids do.

"Could have." That's a guess, Hale, and I don't pay for guesses. Owen wrote this over the weekend, and if you want to argue otherwise you'll need something with a date on it that you can show me. Did you ask him about the paste before the zero went in?
Okay, fair. There's also a quotation in the essay, Hamlet Act 3 Scene 2, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That's not in the play.

Okay. Show me the quotation in the essay and the line you checked against the text. If it's not in the play, that's a factual error in his essay, and a factual error is a mark issue, not a cheating issue. Is that what you're telling me?
I checked it against the text. It's not there.

"Checked it against the text." Okay. Then show me the check: which edition, and where in Act 3 Scene 2 you looked. Write it on paper for me. Right now you have a misquotation, not proof of anything else, and I'm not moving on the zero because of one line. Also, I have a client call at 4:40. It's 4:31.
I used the Folger edition online, searched the whole play. Nothing. I can print it for you.

"Folger, searched the whole play." Okay. Print it, and I'll read it myself. Here's where I am: you've shown me timestamps and one misquotation, and that's a mark conversation, not a zero. Withdraw the zero, put a supervised rewrite on the table, and it stays private, out of his class, with nothing on his record. Put that in writing to me tonight, and I'll decide whether I'm going upstairs.
On the outline, October 15, Owen argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The final essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.

"October 15, the outline." Okay. Show it to me. Is that the outline he handed in, dated, with his name on it? If it is, that's the first thing today that compares his own work to his own work, and I'll read it properly. Turn it toward me.
When I talked to him on November 2, I asked what epistemological paralysis means. He said 'like, being stuck'.

Okay. "Being stuck." That's Owen talking to you, not a document, and I'm writing it down as exactly what it is. Now, is the outline in front of you or not? If it's the handed-in outline dated October 15, with cowardice in it and nothing about paralysis, that's a real change in his argument, and I'd want to know what you think caused it. But you still haven't turned it toward me.
And he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about.

"Couldn't tell you which scene." Okay. That's a question he failed in a hallway, not evidence, and I'm not going to let you put a seventeen-year-old on trial in a conversation. Turn the outline toward me. Then tell me whether you asked him about the zero before it went in, because that's the question the procedure asks, and you still haven't answered it.
I'd say he was nervous, probably, but it looked like he didn't know his own essay.

"Probably." "Looked like." Okay. I'm not building a case on what you thought you saw in a hallway. You have an outline dated October 15 that argues something different from the essay, and I'll look at that. The rest is impressions, and I've told you what I do with impressions. Turn the outline toward me now. It's 4:34.
Here, the outline. Cowardice thesis, his name, October 15. I'm pushing it across the desk.

I'm reading it. Cowardice thesis, his name, October 15. Okay. That's a real difference between the outline and the essay, and I'm writing it down. It still doesn't show who wrote the essay or when. So here are my terms. Withdraw the zero in writing tonight. Any rewrite is supervised, private, not in front of his class, and nothing goes on his record. You put that in an email to me and cc the principal by Thursday. If it isn't in my inbox by then, I'm going upstairs.
And his in-class writing from September 24. 40 minutes, 380 words, he got 62%. Comma splices throughout, no quotations at all.

"September 24. Forty minutes, 380 words, 62 percent." Okay. I'm writing that down. Comma splices and no quotations is a weak sample, and it cuts both ways: it tells me his writing has been rough, which doesn't make a 1,400-word essay written in one night less his. If you want that sample to count, you'll need to show me it's in his handwriting and in his voice, not just a grade in a book. Are you asking me to accept the September piece as proof, or as a comparison? Pick one.
The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Okay. Then you have a different-looking essay from the September piece, and I'd want that explained by something other than the zero. Owen can get better in six weeks, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. But I'm not going to argue about his style with you. The terms are the same: zero withdrawn tonight, supervised private rewrite, nothing on his record, in writing by Thursday. It's 4:37, and I have a call.
No, I did not ask him about the zero before I entered it. That was wrong. I talked to him the day before for five minutes, but I didn't give him the chance to explain the paste.

"Five minutes the day before, and no chance to explain the paste." Okay. That's the first clean admission you've made, and I'm writing it down. It's also the reason the zero should come off the book. Withdraw it tonight, put the terms in writing to me, and cc the principal by Thursday. I'm not moving further on a paste timestamp and a misquotation. It's 4:38.
I can't withdraw the zero tonight without the rewrite. What I can offer is the supervised rewrite, and if he passes it the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

"The rewrite replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record." Okay. That's procedure 4.4, and it's close to what I need, so I'll take it. Three conditions. It's private, not in front of his class. Nothing about the zero or this meeting goes in his file, and you put that in writing. And the rewrite happens within the week, not after his December 1 deadline. Agree to those and I'll put my position in writing to you tonight. Say yes or no.
Can you stay a few more minutes? I know about your call.
"A few more minutes" doesn't change my answer. It's 4:39. Yes or no on the three conditions: private, nothing in his file, and done before December 1.
Is Owen working on anything else at the moment? Does he have a job?
That's not on the table, Hale. He works, and that's our business, not yours. Yes or no on the three conditions. It's 4:40 and I'm going.
Fine. Look, the rewrite is your best path. Will you bring him in Monday at lunch?

Monday at lunch, private, with the zero off the book until he's rewritten it. Put that in an email to me tonight, cc the principal, with nothing about this meeting in his file. If the terms are wrong, say so now.
